what: R1-cpp anchor-hop α/θ calibration sweep on the C++ TRAIN split (GATE_DECISION_r1cpp.md: train = bench/cppbench SFML, held-out = bench/multiswe C++; calibrate on train ONLY)
dataset: bench/cppbench dataset.lock — SFML @ a91a7f6a, n=120 mined / 115 scored, single repo, commit-message queries
harness: bench/cppbench/run_cppbench.py --arms for (top-k 200); binary = audit5r2-r1cpp build (R1 patch + MaxScore-pruning restoration, ea03181)
baseline: same binary with RIPWIRE_NO_ANCHORHOP=1 (gate-proven byte-identical to a main-built binary on the conceptual route)
determinism_note: every arm run is verified byte-identical twice by the harness; single-run sweep points are exact, not sampled
deviation_logged: the pre-registered α grid {0.05..0.40} had its strict@10 maximum ON the boundary (α=0.40), so the TRAIN-side grid was extended to {0.50, 0.60, 0.80} before choosing — this touches train only (held-out untouched) and is logged per the GATE doc's deviation rule; the extension confirms 0.40 is a genuine interior maximum (decline to +2.61 / +0.87 / −0.87)
rationale: pre-registered selection rule applied mechanically: maximize train strict@10 (α=0.40, +3.48pp, unique max) → θ ties on strict@10 (0.25/0.50/0.75 all +3.48) → @1/MRR tiebreak picks θ=0.75 (+0.87pp @1, MRR +0.0148 vs +0.0125). Note the C++ surface has NO α damage region below 0.8 (unlike Python, where α=0.40 was −1.58pp strict@10 with monotone @1/MRR damage) — consistent with the R1-cpp premise that call-graph evidence is denser in C++.
python_risk_noted_before_heldout: the Python train sweep (anchorhop_calib.json) measured α=0.40 at −1.58pp strict@10 on LocBench train — the pre-registered Python no-regression guard is therefore expected to be at genuine risk at these constants; per the GATE doc's decision tree that outcome ships as opt-in (default off), not always-on. Recorded here BEFORE the held-out or guard runs.
